mechanism_claims.claim_text: Tat peptide and arginine-enriched Tat variants inhibit HIV-1 IIIB infection in P4-R5 MAGI reporter cells in a concentration-dependent phenotype assay.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Tat peptide; TPvar1; TPvar2; TPvar3; R-10

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=10:3.1. Tat Peptide Inhibits HIV-1 Infection

mechanism_claims.limitations: Reporter-cell infection inhibition is direct antiviral phenotype evidence, not a direct receptor-binding or molecular entry-mechanism assay.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Higher cationic charge in Tat peptide variants is associated with lower EC50 values against HIV-1 IIIB in this assay series.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: TPvar1; TPvar2; TPvar3; R-10 compared with Tat peptide

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=11:3.2. Additional Cationic Charges Increase the Antiviral Potency of Tat Peptide

mechanism_claims.limitations: The paper supports an association between cationic charge and potency; it does not map a molecular binding site for the peptide variants.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The discussion frames Tat/Tat peptide antiviral activity in the context of prior CXCR4-antagonism observations for full-length Tat and cationic inhibitors, but this paper does not directly measure peptide-CXCR4 binding.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Tat peptide family in this paper
mechanism_claims.limitations: Preserved as mechanism context only; not promoted to direct_mechanism.

mechanism_summary: Accepted with cautions: the paper supports antiviral phenotype and a charge-potency association, but no direct peptide-CXCR4 binding, membrane translocation, or molecular entry mechanism assay is present in local material.
